extracted.intended_audience: authors of Cochrane systematic reviews (review teams preparing intervention reviews)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for starting and planning a Cochrane systematic review of interventions, including question formulation, protocol development, team composition, search and synthesis planning, risk-of-bias and GRADE procedures, and quality assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize bias via pre-specified methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic reviews aim to minimize bias through the use of pre-specified research questions and methods that are documented in protocols, and by basing their findings on reliable research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A systematic review attempts to collate all the empirical evidence that fits pre-specified eligibility criteria ... It uses explicit, systematic methods that are selected with a view to minimizing bias, thus providing more reliable findings from which conclusions can be drawn and decisions made. Systematic review methodology sets out a highly structured, transparent and reproducible methodology: the a priori specification of a research question; clarity on the scope of the review and which studies are eligible for inclusion; making every effort to find all relevant research and to ensure that issues of bias in included studies are accounted for; and analysing the included studies in order to draw conclusions based on all the identified research in an impartial and objective way.

rubrics_metrics.name: A priori specification of the review question (use PICO)
rubrics_metrics.description: The review question should be specified a priori; for intervention questions the PICO approach (Population, Intervention, Comparison(s), Outcome) is usually used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Getting the research question right is critical. Reviews may have additional questions (implementation, economic, equity, patient experience). Question formulation should be informed by people with various relevant perspectives so the review addresses important questions to those who will use it. The review question should determine the methods used in the review, and not vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity on scope and eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Define clearly the scope of the review and which studies are eligible for inclusion (participants, comparators, outcomes, and any other eligibility dimensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The protocol sets out context and foundational elements including definition of eligibility criteria such as study participants and the choice of comparators and outcomes. Eligibility criteria may also be defined following development of a logic model to explain how the intervention might work. Details of planned analyses, including investigations of variability across studies, should be specified in the protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive, unbiased searching (MECIR C19: Planning the search)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan in advance the methods to be used for identifying studies: design searches to capture as many studies as possible that meet the eligibility criteria, ensuring relevant time periods and sources are covered and not restricted by language or publication status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searches should be motivated directly by the eligibility criteria. Restricting by publication status or language can introduce publication bias or language bias. Removing language restrictions in English-language databases is not a substitute for searching non-English journals/databases. To reduce reporting bias, searching may need to include unpublished sources of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan assessment of risk of bias (MECIR C20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan in advance the methods to be used for assessing risk of bias in included studies, including the tool(s) to be used, how they will be implemented, and the criteria used to assign judgements (e.g. low, high, unclear).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predefining methods and criteria is important because analysis or interpretation may be affected by the judgements. For randomized trials, use of the Cochrane risk-of-bias tool is Mandatory; it is sufficient to refer to the Handbook definitions of low/unclear/high risk of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan synthesis and statistical methods (MECIR C21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan in advance methods to synthesise results, including whether a quantitative synthesis is planned, how heterogeneity will be assessed, choice of effect measure, and methods for meta-analysis (e.g. inverse variance or Mantel–Haenszel, fixed-effect or random-effects model).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predefining synthesis methods, particularly statistical methods, is important because analysis or interpretation of the review findings may be affected by post hoc judgements made during analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predefine subgroup analyses (MECIR C22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Predefine potential effect modifiers for subgroup analyses at the protocol stage; restrict the number and provide rationale for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specification reduces the risk that many undirected subgroup analyses will lead to spurious explanations of heterogeneity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan GRADE assessment and 'Summary of findings' table (MECIR C23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan in advance methods to assess the certainty of the body of evidence and summarise findings; predefine the choice of important outcomes for the Summary of findings table (typically up to seven) and the methods for GRADE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcomes should include essential outcomes for decision making and generally should not include surrogate or interim outcomes. Choice of outcomes should not be based on anticipated or observed magnitude of effect or because they are likely to have been addressed in included studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish and register a protocol; avoid post hoc changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and publish a protocol and register the review (e.g. PROSPERO); methods should be established and documented in advance, and changes should not be made based on how they affect results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication and registration reduce duplication, promote accountability, and allow peer review of planned methods. While changes can be necessary, they should not be made based on their impact on results; any changes must be transparently declared. All Cochrane Protocols are published in the CDSR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use protocol to minimize bias and plan resources
rubrics_metrics.description: A protocol reduces the impact of authors' biases, promotes transparency, reduces duplication, allows peer review of methods, and helps plan resources and logistics for the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because review authors' prior knowledge may influence choices (question, eligibility, outcomes), preparing a protocol written without knowledge of available studies reduces bias. Two exceptions to retrospective nature are prospectively planned meta-analyses of series of trials and some living systematic reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition: include both topic and methodological expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic reviews should be undertaken by a team that includes domain expertise and methodological expertise (including statistical expertise); Cochrane will not publish a review proposed to be undertaken by a single person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Team working spreads effort and ensures tasks (selection, data extraction, rating certainty) are performed by at least two people independently, minimizing errors. Topic expertise should not be overly narrow and different disciplinary perspectives are valuable. Methodological expertise provides non-content expertise to counter prior-knowledge bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent duplicate work for critical tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Key tasks such as selection of studies for eligibility, data extraction and rating the certainty of the evidence should be performed by at least two people independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent assessment reduces the likelihood of errors. Review management software can record independent assessments and enable later checks. Research shows even experienced reviewers make mistakes and disagree on risk-of-bias assessments, so maintaining quality assurance is important despite time costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid and manage conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Review teams and authors should be free of potential conflicts of interest; authors should make complete declarations of interest before registration and refresh them annually until publication and just prior to publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding of Cochrane reviews by commercial organizations with an interest in the outcome is not permitted. Employment, holding patents and other financial support may prevent people joining an author team. Consult Cochrane's Conflict of Interest Policy and update declarations when circumstances change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involve consumers and stakeholders in question formulation and throughout the review
rubrics_metrics.description: People affected by decisions around interventions should be involved in important decisions about the review; consumers (patients, carers, representatives, public) and other stakeholders (policy makers, funders, clinicians) should be engaged to increase relevance and uptake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods include surveys, workshops, focus groups, advisory groups. Advisory group membership should reflect the breadth of the question, consider vulnerable/marginalised people, and may require templates (terms of reference, job descriptions). Provide support (reimbursement, training) and clarity about expectations. Consumer involvement improves applicability to decision makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use advisory groups and appropriate methods to engage wider perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: When stakeholders cannot become authors, involve them via advisory groups or other formats to bring a wider range of perspectives to key decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review team should coordinate advisory input through the process; maintain input throughout to ensure relevance; consider resource availability when choosing engagement methods; templates and resources (INVOLVE, Patient and public page) are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to MECIR expectations and PRISMA-aligned reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply Cochrane's methodological expectations for conduct, reporting and updating of systematic reviews (MECIR) and Plain Language Expectations for Authors of Cochrane Summaries; reporting expectations incorporate PRISMA recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each expectation has a title, rationale and elaboration and is classified as 'mandatory' or 'highly desirable'. Mandatory items are expected to be applied or justified; failure may be a basis for not publishing in CDSR. Identify which expectations are relevant at specific review stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure replicable data management and an auditable record
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain records of inclusion decisions, data collection, transformations or adjustments to establish a secure and retrievable audit trail so reviews are replicable and auditable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good data management processes help avoid loss of data, identify and correct errors, and support updates. Use review management software (Covidence, EPPI-Reviewer) to assist data management and maintain standardized records accessible to team members globally. All review data, including initial eligibility decisions, have value beyond the individual review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design searches and methods driven by eligibility criteria, not vice versa
rubrics_metrics.description: Searches and other methods should be motivated directly by the eligibility criteria for the review; the review question should determine the methods used, not the other way around.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps avoid selecting methods that fit available studies rather than the question. Pre-specify methods to reduce susceptibility to bias from post hoc choices such as excluding selected studies or changing statistical analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about necessary protocol changes
rubrics_metrics.description: While protocol adherence is intended, changes may be necessary; such changes must not be made based on their effect on results and should be transparently declared with rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Just as with randomized trials, protocol changes may respond to unanticipated circumstances, but post hoc decisions made when impact on results is known are highly susceptible to bias and should be avoided unless reasonable grounds exist; declare changes publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose outcomes for decision-making relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Select and predefine outcomes that are essential for decision making (typically up to seven) and avoid relying on surrogate or interim outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Summary of findings table should include essential outcomes; choice should not be influenced by anticipated or observed effect sizes or because outcomes are likely to be reported in included studies.
